subject: Literature
title: Martin Luther and the Power of Print
description: A 60-second lesson on Martin Luther and the Power of Print.

hook.text: Martin Luther's banned writings spread so fast across Europe that the Church could not suppress them in time.

buildup.text: The printing press, invented just decades earlier, let Luther's Ninety-Five Theses reach millions before censors reacted.

discovery.text: Within two weeks, his protest had been copied and distributed across all of Germany without his permission.

twist.text: The Church burned his books publicly, but each burning only increased demand for new copies to be printed.

climax.text: Luther's case proved that new technology can make censorship impossible by letting ideas outrun the censors.

punchline.text: The printing press made banning books a losing battle.

quiz.question: Why was the Church unable to suppress Luther's writings?
options: The printing press spread his ideas faster than censors could react
The Pope secretly agreed with Luther
